title: Original Petition for Personal Injury
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-45678

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS

MARY THERESA O’NEIL-SMITH, PLAINTIFF

v.

GLOBAL FREIGHT SOLUTIONS, INC., DEFENDANT

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, MARY THERESA O’NEIL-SMITH, Plaintiff, complaining of GLOBAL FREIGHT SOLUTIONS, INC., Defendant, and respectfully shows the Court as follows:

I. DISCOVERY CONTROL PLAN

1. Plaintiff requests that discovery be conducted under Level 2 of Rule 190 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.

II. PARTIES

2. Plaintiff Mary Theresa O’Neil-Smith is an individual who resides in Harris County, Texas. Her date of birth is March 14, 1978. Her Social Security Number is 458-12-9876. Her phone number is (713) 555-0198. Her email is mary.oneil-smith@example.com.

3. Defendant Global Freight Solutions, Inc. is a corporation doing business in Texas and may be served with process through its registered agent, John R. Martinez, at 1200 Commerce Street, Houston, Texas 77002.

III. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

4. The subject incident occurred in Harris County, Texas, and jurisdiction and venue are proper in this Court.

IV. FACTS

5. On or about June 12, 2024, Plaintiff was driving her vehicle on Interstate 10 near the exit for Main Street when a tractor-trailer owned by Defendant, negligently operated by its employee, ran a red light and collided with Plaintiff’s car.[1]

6. As a result of the collision, Plaintiff suffered serious bodily injuries, including a fractured femur and a traumatic brain injury. She incurred substantial medical expenses and has experienced loss of earning capacity.

7. Defendant’s negligence was the proximate cause of Plaintiff’s injuries. Defendant failed to properly train and supervise its driver, and failed to maintain its vehicle in a safe condition.

V. DAMAGES

8. Plaintiff seeks damages for: (a) past and future medical expenses; (b) past and future pain and suffering; (c) lost wages and loss of earning capacity; (d) physical impairment; (e) disfigurement; and (f) all other relief to which she is entitled.

VI. PRESUIT DISCOVERY

9. Plaintiff has complied with all conditions precedent, including providing notice to Defendant as required by law.

VII. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays that Defendant be cited to appear and answer herein, and that upon final hearing, Plaintiff have judgment against Defendant for damages, interest, costs of suit, and such other relief as the Court deems just.

Respectfully submitted,

___________________________
Attorney for Plaintiff
JANE A. THOMPSON
State Bar No. 24012345
Thompson & Associates, PLLC
500 Main Street, Suite 300
Houston, Texas 77002
(713) 555-0177
jane.thompson@lawfirm.com

[1] This incident was also the subject of a prior investigation by the Texas Department of Public Safety, report number 2024-3345.

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I hereby certify that a true and correct copy of the foregoing was served on counsel for Defendant on this date.

___________________________
JANE A. THOMPSON

title: Original Petition for Breach of Contract
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-78912

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS

BRIGHTSTAR CONSTRUCTION GROUP, INC., PLAINTIFF

v.

JAMES R. HOLLOWAY-BECKER, DEFENDANT

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, Brightstar Construction Group, Inc., Plaintiff, complaining of James R. Holloway-Becker, Defendant, and states as follows:

I. DISCOVERY PLAN

1. Plaintiff intends to conduct discovery under Level 2 of Rule 190.

II. PARTIES

2. Plaintiff is a Texas corporation with its principal place of business in Dallas County, Texas.

3. Defendant James R. Holloway-Becker is an individual who resides in Dallas County, Texas, and may be served at 4520 Maple Avenue, Apartment 12, Dallas, Texas 75219.

III. JURISDICTION

4. The contract at issue was to be performed in Dallas County, Texas, and this Court has jurisdiction.

IV. FACTS

5. On January 15, 2024, Plaintiff and Defendant entered into a written contract (the “Agreement”) whereby Plaintiff agreed to construct a commercial office building at 789 Elm Street, Dallas, Texas, for a total price of $2,500,000.[1] Defendant agreed to make progress payments as specified in the Agreement.

6. Plaintiff performed all obligations under the Agreement, but Defendant failed to pay the final installment of $250,000 despite repeated demands.

7. As a direct result, Plaintiff has suffered damages in the amount of $250,000, plus interest and attorney’s fees.

V. CAUSES OF ACTION

8. Defendant breached the Agreement by failing to pay the amount due.

9. Plaintiff also seeks recovery under the equitable doctrine of quantum meruit.

VI. ATTORNEY’S FEES

10. Plaintiff is entitled to recover reasonable attorney’s fees under the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, § 38.001, because this is a claim for services rendered.

VII. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests judgment against Defendant for the amount of $250,000, pre-judgment and post-judgment interest, costs, attorney’s fees, and such other relief as the Court deems proper.

Respectfully submitted,

___________________________
Attorney for Plaintiff
PATRICIA M. VANCE
State Bar No. 24056789
Vance & Associates, P.C.
2000 Ross Avenue, Suite 100
Dallas, Texas 75201
(214) 555-0142
p.vance@vancelaw.com

[1] The Agreement is attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated by reference.

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that on this day a copy of the foregoing was served on counsel for Defendant.

___________________________
PATRICIA M. VANCE

title: Original Petition for Negligence
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-11223

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS

SOPHIA R. ALVAREZ, PLAINTIFF

v.

HILL COUNTRY MEDICAL CENTER, LLC, DEFENDANT

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, Sophia R. Alvarez, Plaintiff, complaining of Hill Country Medical Center, LLC, Defendant, and in support states:

I. PARTIES

1. Plaintiff Sophia R. Alvarez is an individual residing in Travis County, Texas. Her date of birth is September 3, 1985. Her Social Security Number is 512-44-7788. Her phone number is (512) 555-0133. Her email is sophia.alvarez@example.com.

2. Defendant Hill Country Medical Center, LLC is a limited liability company operating a hospital in Austin, Texas, and may be served through its registered agent, Nancy O’Neil, at 900 Hospital Drive, Austin, Texas 78704.

II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

3. The events giving rise to this claim occurred in Travis County, Texas.

III. FACTS

4. On November 20, 2023, Plaintiff was admitted to Defendant’s facility for surgery. During the post-operative period, Defendant’s staff negligently administered medication, resulting in an overdose that caused Plaintiff to suffer cardiac arrest and irreversible brain damage.[1]

5. Plaintiff has incurred medical expenses exceeding $1,000,000 and will require lifelong care.

IV. NEGLIGENCE

6. Defendant, through its agents and employees, breached the standard of care by: (a) failing to verify the dosage; (b) failing to monitor Plaintiff; and (c) failing to follow established protocols.

V. DAMAGES

7. Plaintiff seeks damages for past and future medical care, pain, suffering, loss of enjoyment of life, and loss of earning capacity.

VI. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays for judgment against Defendant for all damages recoverable by law, plus interest and costs.

Respectfully submitted,

___________________________
Attorney for Plaintiff
DANIEL K. RODRIGUEZ
State Bar No. 24011234
Rodriguez & Cruz, LLP
500 Congress Avenue, Suite 500
Austin, Texas 78701
(512) 555-0155
d.rodriguez@rc-law.com

[1] The incident was reported to the Texas Medical Board.

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a copy of the foregoing was served on counsel for Defendant.

___________________________
DANIEL K. RODRIGUEZ

title: Original Petition for Employment Discrimination
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-33456

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF BEXAR COUNTY, TEXAS

CARLOS M. HERNANDEZ, PLAINTIFF

v.

TEXAS UTILITIES POWER & LIGHT, INC., DEFENDANT

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, Carlos M. Hernandez, Plaintiff, complaining of Texas Utilities Power & Light, Inc., Defendant, and states:

I. PARTIES

1. Plaintiff Carlos M. Hernandez is an individual residing in Bexar County, Texas. His date of birth is July 22, 1970. His Social Security Number is 612-33-4455. His phone number is (210) 555-0121. His email is carlos.hernandez@example.com.

2. Defendant Texas Utilities Power & Light, Inc. is a corporation doing business in Texas, with its principal office in San Antonio, Texas.

II. JURISDICTION

3. The employment practices complained of occurred in Bexar County.

III. FACTS

4. Plaintiff was employed by Defendant from 2005 until his wrongful termination on March 1, 2024. During his tenure, Plaintiff consistently received positive performance reviews.

5. In January 2024, Plaintiff complained to his supervisor about racial discrimination in promotion decisions. Shortly thereafter, he was terminated under the pretext of “restructuring.” [1]

6. Defendant’s actions were motivated by Plaintiff’s race and in retaliation for his complaint, in violation of the Texas Commission on Human Rights Act, Texas Labor Code § 21.051.

IV. DAMAGES

7. Plaintiff seeks back pay, front pay, emotional distress damages, punitive damages, and attorney’s fees.

V. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff requests judgment against Defendant for all damages allowed by law, plus interest and costs.

Respectfully submitted,

___________________________
Attorney for Plaintiff
REBECCA L. TURNER
State Bar No. 24099887
Turner & Associates, P.C.
800 Broadway, Suite 200
San Antonio, Texas 78215
(210) 555-0166
r.turner@turner-law.com

[1] Plaintiff exhausted his administrative remedies with the Texas Workforce Commission and EEOC.

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I hereby certify that a copy of the foregoing was served on Defendant’s counsel.

___________________________
REBECCA L. TURNER

title: Original Petition for Product Liability
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-55678

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TARRANT COUNTY, TEXAS

JOHN DOE AND JANE DOE, INDIVIDUALLY AND AS NEXT FRIENDS OF MINOR CHILD, PLAINTIFFS

v.

ALL-TERRAIN EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURING, CO., DEFENDANT

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, John Doe and Jane Doe, Plaintiffs, complaining of All-Terrain Equipment Manufacturing, Co., Defendant, and respectfully alleges:

I. PARTIES

1. Plaintiffs are residents of Tarrant County, Texas. Defendant is a corporation with its principal place of business in Ohio, but it does business in Texas and may be served through its registered agent, Robert K. Anderson, at 1000 Industrial Park, Fort Worth, Texas 76102.

2. Plaintiff John Doe’s date of birth is April 10, 1980, and his Social Security Number is 712-55-6677. Plaintiff Jane Doe’s date of birth is November 2, 1982. Their phone is (817) 555-0144, email is doe.family@example.com.

II. JURISDICTION

3. This Court has jurisdiction because the injury occurred in Tarrant County.

III. FACTS

4. On September 5, 2023, Plaintiff John Doe was using a Model X-500 all-terrain vehicle manufactured by Defendant. The vehicle suddenly lost braking capability and overturned, causing serious injuries to John and their minor child, who was a passenger.[1]

5. The ATV was defectively designed because the braking system was prone to failure due to a manufacturing flaw.

IV. CAUSES OF ACTION

6. Defendant is liable under theories of strict liability, negligence, and breach of warranty. The defective condition was a producing cause of Plaintiffs’ injuries.

V. DAMAGES

7. Plaintiffs seek damages for medical expenses, pain, suffering, loss of earning capacity, and for the minor child’s injuries.

VI. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiffs pray for judgment against Defendant for all damages, interest, costs, and such other relief as the Court deems proper.

Respectfully submitted,

___________________________
Attorney for Plaintiffs
STEVEN M. CARTER
State Bar No. 24033456
Carter & Nguyen, LLP
1500 Main Street, Suite 400
Fort Worth, Texas 76102
(817) 555-0139
s.carter@carter-nguyen.com

[1] The incident was investigated by the Consumer Product Safety Commission.

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a copy of the foregoing was served on counsel for Defendant.

___________________________
STEVEN M. CARTER
